To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) exploiting interoperator parallelisms for multi-join queries can lead to significant speedups; (2) the proposed join sequence heuristics can lead to join sequences that can achieve significant speedups; and (3) the synchronous execution time concept can be applied to the allocation of processors to exploit interoperator parallelism.

(1) exploiting interoperator parallel execution can reduce query execution time by 50% or more, and (2), the two-step approach is the best solution to achieve the goal of exploiting interoperator execution.

(1) the proposed join sequence heuristic is simple and effective, and (2), among all the schemes evaluated in this thesis, the two-step heuristic proposed emerges as the best scheme to minimize query execution time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of exploiting interoperator, or join, parallelism in a multi-join query.
the optimization of parallel execution for multi-join queries in a shared-memory multiprocessor environment.
the optimization of multi-join query execution in a parallel database system with multiple processors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two-step approach, in conjunction with a good join sequence, can lead to the optimal query execution time, while the bottom-up approaches, which do not take the join sequence into account, are inferior in performance.
the proposed two-step approach is a simple and effective method to optimize the parallel execution of multi-joins.
the proposed heuristic approaches to both issues (1)and (2) can lead to an efficient execution of multi- join queries on a parallel system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by using the two-step approach, one can obtain a bushy tree with a join sequence that is close to the optimal, and then can allocate processors to the join operations in the bushy to minimize the execution time.
, by exploiting the interoperator parallelism, a multi-join query could be executed faster than the sequential execution of each join.

the two-step approach can achieve a speedup factor of 1.5-3.0 for the execution of a query with up to 20 joins on an 8-processor system, compared with the execution of the query on a single processor system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to optimize the query execution time, the interoperator parallelism can be exploited in the same way that the intraoperator parallelism has been exploited.
the proposed heuristic methods are simple and effective in exploiting interoperator parallel execution for multi-join queries in parallel database systems.

, for a multi-join query, the exploitation of interoperator parallelism can significantly outperform the exploitation of intraoperator parallelisms, and the two-step approach is a good solution to optimize the parallel execution of multi-joins.
